old: The Essive-Formal Case Suffix: -ként ('as, in the capacity of')
new: Recap: -ként for a Role
why: the screen presents a form an earlier unit taught as new; rewritten as a recap (essive-formal-kent, a2-176-a)

old: The suffix *-ként* expresses role, capacity, or form ('as / in the capacity of / like'): *tanárként dolgozik* ('works as a teacher'), *példaként említi* ('mentions as an example'). Unlike *-ul/-ül*, *-ként* attaches without vowel harmony changes directly to stems.
new: You know the essive-formal *-ként* from A2 Unit 36 (*tanárként*, *diákként*): it says in which role or capacity someone acts, and it never changes with vowel harmony. Here you use it for roles in society: *Állampolgárként mindannyian felelősek vagyunk a közösségünkért.*
why: the screen presents a form an earlier unit taught as new; rewritten as a recap (essive-formal-kent, a2-176-a)

old: While *mint* is often used with nominative or inflected nouns (*úgy él, mint egy király* - 'lives like a king'), *-ként* strictly designates function or role (*vezetőként hozott döntést* - 'made a decision as a leader').
new: *-ként* says in which role someone acts: *vezetőként hozott döntést* = he made a decision as a leader (he is the leader). *mint* compares: *úgy él, mint egy király* = he lives like a king (but is not one). Compare *Anna tanárként dolgozik* (Anna is a teacher) with *Anna úgy dolgozik, mint egy tanár* (she works like a teacher, but is not one).
why: the rule said -ként "strictly" marks a role and mint is used with nouns; it gave no contrast pair that shows the difference

old: The Distributive Suffix: -nként ('per, by, at intervals')
new: Recap: -nként for \"per\"
why: the screen presents a form an earlier unit taught as new; rewritten as a recap (distributive-nkent, a2-68-b)

old: The suffix *-nként* (or *-anként / -enként / -onként*) indicates distribution per unit or intervals: *fejenként* ('per head / per person'), *havonta / havonként* ('monthly / per month'), *csoportonként* ('by group').
new: You know the distributive *-nként* from A2 Unit 14 (and the time words in *-nta/-nte* from A2 Unit 1): it says how much or how often per person, group or period. After a vowel it is *-nként* (*havonként*, like *havonta*), after a consonant *-onként/-enként/-önként*: *fejenként* (per head), *csoportonként* (by group), *családonként* (per family).
why: the screen presents a form an earlier unit taught as new; rewritten as a recap (distributive-nkent, a2-68-b)

old: To compare two differing realities, use *míg* ('while / whereas') and *ezzel szemben* ('by contrast / in contrast to this'): *A nagyvárosokban több a lehetőség, míg a kistelepüléseken nehezebb a munkahelyteremtés.*
new: You know *míg* from B1 Unit 4 (*while*) and *ezzel szemben* from B1 Unit 21 (*in contrast*). Both also compare two groups or places: *A nagyvárosokban több a lehetőség, míg a kistelepüléseken nehezebb a munkahelyteremtés.*
why: the screen presents a form an earlier unit taught as new; rewritten as a recap (míg B1 Unit 4, adversative-contrast b1-11-03); ezzel ellentétben is a bare extra phrase

old: Evaluative Language: igazságos, méltányos, elfogadhatatlan
new: Recap: Judging Fairness with hogy
why: the screen presents a form an earlier unit taught as new; rewritten as a recap (hogy-jon-jen, b1-03-03-b)

old: Discussing social justice involves evaluative predicate adjectives followed by *hogy*: *Igazságos, hogy minden gyermek jó oktatást kapjon.* ('It is fair that every child receive a good education.'). Negative judgments often use *elfogadhatatlan* ('unacceptable').
new: You know *hogy* + a verb in *-jon/-jen* from B1 Unit 5. After a judgement such as *igazságos* ('fair'), *méltányos* ('equitable') or *elfogadhatatlan* ('unacceptable'), *hogy* introduces what is judged: with *-jon/-jen* it says what should be so (*Igazságos, hogy minden gyermek jó oktatást kapjon.*), with an ordinary verb it states a fact (*Nem tartom méltányosnak, hogy a költségek gyorsan emelkednek.*).
why: the screen presents a form an earlier unit taught as new; rewritten as a recap (hogy-jon-jen, b1-03-03-b)

old: Official welfare descriptions use *részesül vmiben* ('receives / benefits from'): *segélyben részesül* ('receives welfare aid'), *ösztöndíjban részesül* ('receives a scholarship').
new: You know from B1 Unit 21 that some verbs govern *-ban/-ben* (*részt vesz valamiben*). So does *részesül valamiben* ('to receive, to benefit from'): *segélyben részesül* ('receives welfare aid'), *ösztöndíjban részesül* ('receives a scholarship').
why: the screen presents a form an earlier unit taught as new; rewritten as a recap (verb-government-ban-ben, b1-11-05); juttat vmit in the title was never explained

old: To specify civil actors and groups, use demonstrative + relative pairings: *azok az emberek, akik...* ('those people who...'), *olyan kezdeményezések, amelyek...* ('initiatives that...').
new: You know *aki*, *ami* and *amely* from A2 Unit 4 and B1 Unit 10. They also work after *azok a* ('those') and *olyan* ('such'): *azok az emberek, akik…* ('those people who…'), *olyan kezdeményezések, amelyek…* ('initiatives that…').

old: To voice positions on inequality politely and persuasively: *Úgy látom, hogy...* ('As I see it...'), *Véleményem szerint elengedhetetlen...* ('In my view it is indispensable...'), *Nem szabad figyelmen kívül hagynunk...* ('We must not ignore...').

why: the screen presents a form an earlier unit taught as new; rewritten as a recap (szerintem, a2-58-b); Meggyőződésem szerint in the title was an unexplained extra
